sentences.text: Switching coordination begins with a defined operational need, a safe sequence, and an agreed period for execution.
The Duty Planner develops the proposed sequence with the Control Engineer and identifies affected equipment and operating limits.
The Control Engineer checks the current network configuration and confirms that the proposed sequence supports the approved work.
The Substation Operator verifies equipment status and switching points at the Offshore Substation.
The Grid Dispatcher confirms applicable grid requirements and any restrictions on changing the connection state.
A Grid Constraint requires the Duty Planner to reassess the sequence and obtain revised authorization before work proceeds.
The Maintenance Planning Engine provides the planned work period and identifies dependencies with other scheduled tasks.
The Weather Service supplies forecast conditions relevant to access and safe execution.
The Weather Analyst reviews the forecast and advises the Duty Planner if conditions could affect the planned sequence.
The Marine Coordinator aligns vessel movements with the approved access plan and operational constraints.
The Vessel Master confirms that the vessel can meet the agreed timing and maintain safe operating margins.
The Personnel Tracking Console and Work Permit Portal are checked to confirm that assigned personnel and permits are ready.
The HSE Officer reviews task hazards and confirms that required controls are in place before switching is authorized.
The Duty Planner records the proposed sequence, required approvals, execution roles, and planned communications in the operating record.
The Control Engineer prepares clear switching instructions with one action per step and an explicit hold point where needed.
The Electrical Technician verifies equipment labels and confirms the intended switching points before execution.
The Substation Operator accepts the instructions only after checking the equipment state and confirming authorization with the Control Engineer.
The Shore Control Room sends the Switching Window Acknowledgment after the approved switching period is entered in the operating log.
The Substation Operator uses the test trace to verify that the planned restoration checks have completed before requesting the next switching step.
During execution, the switching operator performs each authorized action and reports completion before the next instruction is issued.
The Control Engineer monitors available indications and confirms that each reported state change matches the approved sequence.
If an indication is ambiguous, communications fail, or conditions differ from the plan, the sequence is paused and the equipment is left in a safe state.
The Field Supervisor confirms personnel are clear of affected equipment before the Duty Planner authorizes restoration or release of the work area.
After completion, the Duty Planner records the final equipment state, approvals, deviations, and handover information for the incoming shift.
